text:
Maria: FYI customer (Acme) pushed back asking if we can commit to a 24h breach notification for the POC. They quoted SIG/CAIQ asking for incident notification timelines. Can security/legal weigh in?
Jia: short answer: we can commit to notify stakeholders quickly, but exact SLA depends on deployment mode + confirmation status. details below.
Sam: they're on Hosted for the POC, so managed detection and IR path applies. Maria — can you confirm if PII is in scope?
Maria: Yes, minimal PII in the POC logs, not production.
Jia: ok. For Hosted/Dedicated we operate a 24/7 detection & response pipeline. Our standard practice is: initial acknowledgement to customer contacts within 24 hours of confirming an incident that impacts their data; follow-up updates every 48 hours until resolved; final report + RCA within 30 days (or earlier if available).
Owen: legal note — we should avoid guaranteeing timelines for "suspected" incidents. Contract language should say "confirmed security incident affecting Customer data" to be precise. Also watch regulatory windows (e.g., GDPR 72h notification to regulator) — our customer notification cadence can be faster than regulatory filings but can't force a customer to notify regulators on our timeline.
Jia: for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) we typically provide playbook & remote assistance. Customers control their network & notification obligations; we offer collaboration and forensic artifacts under NDAs.
Sam: for the POC, recommend we offer: 1) initial notification within 24h of confirmation; 2) daily updates until containment; 3) access to redacted logs & packet captures for forensics. That should satisfy the CAIQ checkbox for IR timelines.
Maria: can you suggest exact wording for the SIG/CAIQ answer and a bracketed contract clause we can share with their procurement?
Jia: CAIQ answer (brief): "Yes — vendor maintains a documented Incident Response Plan with defined roles, defined notification timelines for affected customers, escalation procedures, and periodic tabletop exercises. For hosted/dedicated customers we provide initial customer notification within 24 hours of confirmation, with ongoing updates until resolution."
Jia: Contract sample clause (suggested):
````
If Redwood Inference determines there has been a confirmed security incident affecting Customer Data, Redwood will: (a) notify Customer within twenty-four (24) hours of such determination, (b) provide regular updates at least every forty-eight (48) hours until containment, and (c) deliver a post-incident report and root-cause analysis within thirty (30) days, subject to legal constraints. Notifications will be made to the Customer contacts specified in the Ordering Document.
````
Owen: tweak: change "within twenty-four (24) hours of such determination" to "as soon as reasonably practicable and, absent legal restriction, no later than seventy-two (72) hours after confirmation" if customer insists on conservative language. Some enterprise legal teams push back on an absolute 24h promise.
IR-Bot: Incident playbook updated: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/ir — includes notification templates, RCA template, and forensic checklist. :link: :white_check_mark:
Sam: also note retention: we ship logs to S3 for hosted customers for 90 days by default. If Acme needs longer retention for forensics, we can add in SOW.
Jia: preserve evidence guidance: snapshot KV caches, preserve model inputs/outputs metadata, collect GPU kernel logs if requested. We will coordinate with their security team to minimize data exposure.
Maria: great — I'll send them a short email w/ CAIQ blurb + our proposed clause and offer a 30min call with Jia & Owen.
Owen: +1, loop me in on legal review if they countersign.
Sam: thumbs up from engineering side.
Jia: happy to join call and run through our IR timeline and what we can provide for forensics.
Maria: thanks all. I'll post final wording here after the call. :thumbsup:
